{
  "segment_function": "argument",
  "claims": [
    {
      "claim": "The meanings of being indoors or outdoors are not the same for everyone due to factors like global inequality and the varying severities of warming.",
      "claim_type": "author_position",
      "supporting_excerpt": "the meaning of being indoors or outdoors, whether literally or figuratively, will not be the same for everyone, any more than the meaning of a domestic interior is the same for men and women, or for prosperous homeowners and the people they hire to do their cleaning.",
      "support_kind": "direct",
      "qualifications": [
        "partly because warming is likely to have severer consequences sooner in the global South",
        "partly because the shape and availability of these adaptations will depend on existing forms of social inequality, both locally and globally"
      ],
      "confidence": 1
    },
    {
      "claim": "Hannah Arendt tended to abstract from forms of inequality and hierarchy in The Human Condition because of a premise that postwar emancipation, the welfare state, and capitalist abundance meant contemporary unfreedom involved society relating to each member rather than some ruling others.",
      "claim_type": "author_position",
      "supporting_excerpt": "Arendt tended to abstract from the forms of inequality and hierarchy that characterized postwar Europe and America, not to mention — and she didn’t— relations between the global North and the global South.",
      "support_kind": "direct",
      "qualifications": [
        "her tendency to abstract in this way was the upshot of a specific and hugely problematic premise about the shape of the postwar world"
      ],
      "confidence": 1
    }
  ],
  "definitions": [],
  "distinctions": [],
  "examples": [],
  "objections": [],
  "responses": [],
  "references_to_other_sections": [
    "The Human Condition"
  ],
  "unresolved_context": [
    "The conflictual politics of adaptations to climate change and the limits of The Human Condition in addressing the planetary situation."
  ],

    "Asymmetrical impacts of climate adaptation and global inequality.",
    "Limits of Hannah Arendt's framework regarding historical exclusions of inequality and hierarchy."
  ]
}
